fatal_errors: The proposed CoCrFeNiTi alloy contains no Al, so formation of the claimed protective Al2O3 layer is chemically impossible without an unreported source of aluminum.
The falsification logic is reversed: degradation at 1400 °C would support the proposed 1200–1300 °C optimum rather than falsify it.
No cited evidence supports the stated oxidation mass gain, aqueous corrosion rate, density, or self-healing oxide mechanism for CoCrFeNiTi.
The proposed 1200–1300 °C processing window misses the target 800–1000 °C window and ignores magnesium-volatilization constraints central to the target system.
explanation: The response identifies the broad mechanical-alloying-plus-SPS strategy and offers a potentially viable multi-principal alloy, but it does not reconstruct the MgAlTiVFeCo BCC system, the 1000 °C optimum, or the oxide-barrier mechanism involving AlV2O4, FeAl2O4, and FeTiO3. Its service conditions also differ substantially from oxidation at 900 °C in air and corrosion in 3.5 wt% NaCl. E1 supports a nanocrystalline FCC/BCC CoCrFeNiTi alloy and its mechanical properties, but not the asserted SPS window or environmental performance. E2 concerns a different refractory alloy, while E3 concerns AlCoCrFeNi2.1 and cannot validate CoCrFeNiTi oxide or corrosion behavior. The baseline does not isolate sintering-temperature effects, and the proposed experiment neither directly measures the claimed phase/oxide mechanism nor constitutes a valid falsification test.
